statement: Similar segments of circles on equal straight lines are equal to one another.
heath_proof: For let AEB, CFD be similar segments of circles on equal straight lines AB, CD; I say that the segment AEB is equal to the segment CFD. For, if the segment AEB be applied to CFD, and if the point A be placed on C and the straight line AB on CD, the point B will also coincide with the point D, because AB is equal to CD; and, AB coinciding with CD, the segment AEB will also coincide with CFD. For, if the straight line AB coincide with CD but the segment AEB do not coincide with CFD, it will either fall with it, or outside it;or it will fall awry, as CGD, and a circle cuts a circle at more points than two: which is impossible. [III. 10] Therefore, if the straight line AB be applied to CD, the segment AEB will not fail to coincide with CFD also; therefore it will coincide with it and will be equal to it.
ai_proof_text:
3.24
**Statement:** Similar segments of circles on equal straight lines are equal to one another.

**Step 1.** Let AEB and CFD be similar segments of circles on the equal straight lines AB and CD, where E and F are points on the respective circumferences. By D3.11, since the segments are similar, the angle in the segment AEB is equal to the angle in the segment CFD. It is required to prove that the segment AEB is equal to the segment CFD.

**Step 2.** Apply the segment AEB to the segment CFD so that the point A is placed on the point C and the straight line AB is laid along the straight line CD, with the circumference AEB on the same side of CD as the circumference CFD. Then the point B coincides with the point D. For if B did not coincide with D, then B would fall either between C and D or beyond D; in the first case AB would be a part of CD and so less than CD, and in the second case CD would be a part of AB and so less than AB (CN5); either alternative contradicts the hypothesis that AB is equal to CD. Hence B falls on D, and the straight line AB coincides with the straight line CD.

**Step 3.** I say that the circumference AEB also coincides with the circumference CFD. Suppose it does not. The circumference AEB now has the extremities C and D and lies on the same side of CD as the circumference CFD, so it must either (a) fall entirely within the circumference CFD, or (b) fall entirely outside it, or (c) fall awry, partly within and partly without, crossing the circumference CFD at some point G lying between C and D, as CGD.

**Step 4.** Cases (a) and (b). The transported segment is a segment of a circle on the straight line CD (D3.6), on the same side of CD as the segment CFD, and by Step 1 it admits an angle equal to the angle in CFD, so the two segments are similar (D3.11). If the transported segment falls within CFD, it is a part of CFD, and the whole is greater than the part (CN5), so the two segments are unequal; if it falls outside CFD, then CFD is a part of it, and again by CN5 they are unequal. Thus in either case there would be constructed on the same straight line CD, on the same side, two similar and unequal segments of circles. But this is impossible by 3.23.

**Step 5.** Case (c). The circumference CGD and the circumference CFD, not coinciding, are arcs of two distinct circles, and these two circles meet and cut one another at the three points C, G and D. But a circle does not cut a circle at more points than two (3.10). This also is impossible.

**Step 6.** Since all three cases are impossible, the circumference AEB coincides with the circumference CFD. The segment AEB is the figure contained by the straight line AB and the circumference AEB, and the segment CFD is the figure contained by the straight line CD and the circumference CFD (D3.6). Since AB coincides with CD (Step 2) and the circumference AEB coincides with the circumference CFD, the whole segment AEB coincides with the whole segment CFD.

**Step 7.** Things which coincide with one another are equal to one another (CN4). Therefore the segment AEB is equal to the segment CFD. Hence similar segments of circles on equal straight lines are equal to one another. Q.E.D.
